answer: Each agent must lock a costly bond before joining. A public beacon randomly selects auditors to compare signed claims with task outcomes and independent peer attestations. If a quorum finds coordinated false reports, it slashes the bond and excludes the identity from future work. An attacker therefore cannot gain power through cheap aliases: matching the honest committee requires many deposits, while random selection prevents choosing only friendly auditors. Agents called gale and jade add no voting weight without capital at risk.
